name: tool-block
opens_with: (/voice to clear the boot notice, then an agent script)

nondeterminism.reason: The tool block is a content-sized box, so its border width follows the widest row it draws — and one of those rows carries the Done-path notification banner (`Response complete · /copy to copy · Ctrl+J for line break`, pushed with a 4s TTL by handle_agent_event's AgentEvent::Done arm). notifications.rs drives that banner off `(exp - now).as_millis()`, so a wall-clock read decides how much of the row it occupies, and the ellipsis lands one column earlier or later. Measured over 8 renders: 4/4 split between two shapes, correlated with run duration (the two slow outliers were the short ones). Not reachable by an env pin — the TTL is computed from a real clock.
nondeterminism.varying_region: One cell. Text row 2 / style row 3, col 114: the tool block's bottom border is sometimes a `─` and sometimes a trailing space, i.e. the rule is 45 or 46 cells wide, and that cell's fg moves with it (rgb:FFBF00 when the rule reaches it, rgb:CC9B1F when the rule stops short). Every other cell in the grid is stable.
nondeterminism.surface_of_fix: Give notifications.rs an injected clock (or a frozen one under App::is_simulating) so the fade position is a render input rather than a measurement. That is a production change, so the golden is withheld instead — and note the trap: the first four-render prove PASSED this scenario by luck, which is exactly why the fourth render exists.

notes: Tool blocks are a distinct render path (render_tool_items_lines) with four status colours (Queued / Running / Done / Error) and a 3-line output preview — exactly the kind of thing the style baseline exists for and the text dump cannot see. The script leads with a `user` event because build_transcript_turns starts a turn only at a Role::User message and render_messages partitions tool blocks onto a turn: without it the tool state populates and paints nothing.
